specimen.body: A seven-day loop: dictation on Day 1, shadowing on Days 2–6, and a re-dictation on Day 7 to see your progress.

pixelFish.intro: Style: realistic colors, big cute eyes. True-to-life patterns, colors, and light; eyes about 1/3 of the head’s height with one big and one small glint; a slightly rounder, shorter body. They blink now and then and look at the pointer or food; happy ^ ^ after eating; hungry with half-closed lids, slower and lower. Colors, eye size, and other knobs live in lib/pixel-fish/style.ts.
pixelFish.tankLabel: A {name} swimming in a pixel-art aquarium
pixelFish.reduced: Reduced motion is on: the fish stays still, doesn’t blink, and its eyes don’t move. The buttons switch still expressions.
pixelFish.lookHint: Move the pointer or a finger over the tank and the fish looks at it; it watches food as it sinks.
pixelFish.togetherHint: From small to big: snail < clownfish < great white < whale shark. The whale shark is the slowest; the snail creeps along the glass and the floor.
pixelFish.togetherLabel: A snail, a clownfish, a great white, and a whale shark in one pixel-art aquarium
pixelFish.snailNote: Eyes on the tentacle tips; a shell with a logarithmic spiral; creeps along the glass and the floor.
pixelFish.clownfishNote: Three white bands edged in black, black fin margins.
pixelFish.greatWhiteNote: Still a shark: pointed snout, grey back and white belly, gill slits, tall dorsal fin, crescent tail; short and chubby with a little toothy smile.
pixelFish.whaleSharkNote: The biggest and slowest: a broad flat head with a wide front mouth, white spots and faint stripes, white belly.

timing.title: Timing check
timing.intro: Play each sentence and nudge its start and end by 0.1 s. Playback adds the same padding learners hear (0.15 s before, 0.25 s after, never into a neighboring sentence). When it sounds right, copy the JSON and send it to the developer.

timing.tapIntro: Play from a starting point and press Space as each sentence begins (on a phone, press “Sentence starts”); press Enter when the last one ends (or “Last sentence ended”). The taps are applied right away; then play each sentence below to fine-tune.

timing.excerpt: This part's sentences and times come from the full version, so they aren't tuned here. Tune the full version, then ask the developer to run npm run video:sync to copy the times into each part.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: ListenLoop is an English listening practice site. This policy explains what data we collect, how we use it, where it's kept, and how you can delete it. Every practice feature works without signing in.

sections.title: What we collect
paragraphs: Only when you sign in with a Google account do we collect:
items: Account details from Google: email, name, profile picture URL, and Google account ID. Only the email is shown.
Practice data: your progress on each video (which days are done, dictation answers and accuracy, shadowing status) and a daily practice log.
Created practices (admins only for now): the text you type or upload when creating a practice, its sentences and translations, the vocabulary and grammar notes, and the generated audio.

Sharing and reports: anyone can see a public practice's title, sentences, translations, notes, and audio, but not its author's account details. When you report a practice, we keep the reason, your details, and your account ID only to review it; the author isn't told who reported it.
Sign-in state: a sign-in token in a browser cookie.

sections.title: When you're not signed in
paragraphs: Your progress stays in your browser (localStorage) and is never sent to our servers. The interface language is kept in a cookie and the theme in localStorage. Clearing your browser data removes them.

sections.title: How we use it
paragraphs: Only to sign you in and keep your progress in sync across devices. We don't sell data, share it with advertisers, or use advertising or analytics trackers.

sections.title: Where it's kept and who processes it
items: Supabase: the database for accounts and cloud practice data, in the United States (us-east-1).
Vercel: the web host, which handles the technical data a connection needs (such as IP addresses) to serve and protect the site.

Microsoft Azure AI services: when you create a practice, its text is sent to Azure OpenAI (the gpt-5-mini model) to split it into sentences, translate it, and write vocabulary and grammar notes, or to write practice text for the situation you pick; its English sentences go to Azure Speech for audio. Under Microsoft's terms, what's sent and what's generated aren't used to train models. Azure OpenAI may keep them for up to 30 days to detect abuse, and may process them in any of Microsoft's regions (a Global Standard deployment); Azure Speech processes them in the United Arab Emirates. Even so, please don't put personal or sensitive information in practice text.
YouTube: practice videos play through YouTube (youtube-nocookie.com); once a video plays, YouTube may set cookies under Google's privacy policy.

Speech recognition: shadowing uses your browser's built-in speech recognition; in Chrome, audio is sent to Google's servers to be recognized. ListenLoop doesn't record or store audio, only whether each sentence is done and how much was heard.

sections.title: How long we keep it
paragraphs: As long as your account exists. When you delete your account, it and your cloud practice data are deleted from the database right away; any system backups kept by our providers are cleared when they expire.

sections.title: Your choices and rights
items: Sign out at any time; your practice data stays on this device.
On the Account page you can delete your account and cloud data for good, which also clears the practice data on this device.
To ask about or correct your data, contact us as below.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: When this policy changes, we update this page and the date above. Major changes are also announced on the site.

privacy.contact: For privacy questions, post on the project's GitHub page (posts are public, so please leave out personal details; we'll get in touch):
